# crossbearing

> A read-only evidence engine that corroborates what AI agents claim they did
> against the records the infrastructure already keeps — CloudTrail, GCP and
> Azure audit logs, Kubernetes audit, GitHub audit — and emits signed,
> auditor-ready evidence. It runs inside the customer's own cloud account,
> holds no customer data, and cannot write to the environments it reads.

This file is the machine-readable index of the organization's public surface.
Every factual claim below is externally checkable — the licences, the
dependency counts, the paths — and is meant to stay that way.

## Repositories

- [crossbearing/crossbearing](https://github.com/crossbearing/crossbearing):
  the engine. Go. Source-available under the Functional Source License 1.1
  (ALv2 future license) — not an OSI-approved licence, so tooling reports it as
  NOASSERTION rather than a known SPDX id. `./demo/run.sh` produces a full
  divergence report offline in about five seconds.
- [crossbearing/verify](https://github.com/crossbearing/verify): the offline
  Agent Evidence Package verifier. Go, MIT, and **zero dependencies** — the
  standard library is its entire supply chain, enforced in CI by a check that
  fails if `go.sum` exists. It re-derives a package's hash chain and signature
  without importing the engine or contacting crossbearing.
- [crossbearing/scenarios](https://github.com/crossbearing/scenarios): named
  agent misbehaviors in real infrastructure, MIT. Each is a complete arc — the
  evidence, the finding, the fix that closes it, and the proof re-run.
- [crossbearing/.github](https://github.com/crossbearing/.github): the org
  profile and the organization-wide community health defaults.

## The evidence format

`aep/1` is the Agent Evidence Package format the engine emits and the verifier
checks. Findings are hash-chained from a genesis anchored to the report window
and match policy, signed with a KMS key the customer names, and each finding
carries a re-fetchable locator and digest. Edit, reorder, or drop one finding
and every downstream hash changes and the signature stops verifying.

The normative definition lives in the two implementations above rather than in
this file — read [crossbearing/verify](https://github.com/crossbearing/verify)
if you need the format, since it is the smaller of the two and depends on
nothing.

## Policies

- [Security policy](https://github.com/crossbearing/.github/blob/main/SECURITY.md):
  what's in scope, and how to report privately. Evidence integrity,
  attribution correctness, and the read-only guarantee are the areas we most
  want tested.
- [Support](https://github.com/crossbearing/.github/blob/main/SUPPORT.md):
  where to take a question, by kind.
- [Contributing](https://github.com/crossbearing/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md):
  ground rules, including the two product properties — read-only architecture
  and a lean supply chain — that a change must not break.
- [Code of conduct](https://github.com/crossbearing/.github/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md):
  Contributor Covenant 2.1.

## Optional

- [crossbearing.dev](https://crossbearing.dev): the product site and the
  five-minute divergence demo.
